title: Region-aware progressive fidelity degradation and admission controller
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During cross-region spikes and partial regional outages we observe cascaded latency increases and elevated error rates as requests flood failover regions. We need an admission and degradation strategy that keeps SLOs for high-priority tenants while maximizing useful throughput for best-effort traffic.

Goal: Implement a region-aware admission controller that applies progressive fidelity degradation per-request based on tenant SLA, model family, sequence-length distribution, and regional capacity signals. Integrate this with regional circuit breakers and a soft quota-borrowing mechanism so failover regions can accept limited overflow without violating reserved capacity SLOs.

Proposal summary:
- Admission controller computes a dynamic admission decision using: region_capacity_score, tenant_priority_band, per-tenant quota_balance, model_cost_estimate (tokens * cost_per_token for model variant), and kv_cache_hotness (recent prefix hit ratio).
- Progressive fidelity degradation ladder (highest->lowest fidelity): full model (top-tier variant) -> quantized variant (int8/4) -> short-context condensed generation (max_tokens cap and early stopping heuristics) -> hybrid (embedding + canned summary) -> degrade to best-effort background queue with eventual callback or 202 response.
- Probabilistic thinning for P2/P3 tenants: at 80-95% regional saturation, scale down acceptance probability instead of pure drop to avoid synchronized spikes. Thinning parameters are per-tenant class and warmed by historical acceptance curves.
- Regional soft-borrowing: allow N% of requests from failing region to be accepted in target region under a controlled budget window; when borrowed budget exhausts, further traffic is locally thinned, not routed. Borrowing is limited by a safety-cap tied to reserved capacity for P0/P1 tenants.
- Circuit breaker triggers: cognitive latency-based (p95 RTT > threshold), error-rate slope (5m error-rate doubling), and queue-depth thresholds. When tripped, apply aggressive degradation for non-P0 traffic and immediately start quota-borrowing signals upstream.
- Observability: add per-request admission_reason labels, degradation_level, borrowed_region tag, and kv_cache_hit boolean to traces. Expose dashboards for borrowed_budget, admitted_by_fidelity, and per-tenant accepted_vs_rejected curves.

Why different from previous work: several existing tickets focus on priority queues and token-bucket policies. This ticket combines multi-region awareness, kv-cache-informed admission hints, progressive fidelity ladder (including embedding+canned fallback), and a soft-borrowing budget to smooth failovers rather than immediate shedding.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller evaluates and returns one of: {accept_full, accept_quantized, accept_condensed, accept_embedding_fallback, queue_with_callback, reject} for each request and annotates RPC trace with admission_reason and degradation_level.
Canary rollout in eu-west-1 accepting borrowed traffic from ap-southeast-1 with borrowed_budget telemetry; borrowed budget replenishes and decays as configured and is visible on dashboard.

Automated test harness simulating regional outage and spike demonstrates: P0 tenant p95 latency preserved within SLO, total useful throughput increased vs current baseline by >=8% during failover windows.
Circuit breaker triggers result in immediate downgrade of non-P0 traffic and emit runbook notification; breakers auto-recover when metrics return below thresholds for configured cooldown window.
No regression in latency for normal steady-state traffic in primary region (p99 increase < 5% vs baseline).
implementation_notes: Admission decision will live in serving front-end layer (admission service) to minimize added hop latency. Keep decision logic lightweight (O(1) with cached tenant bands) and use Redis for per-tenant quota_balances and borrowed_budget counters.
KV cache hotness computed as exponential moving average of prefix_hit_ratio over 1m windows; use this as a hint to prefer accepting requests that are cache-warm with higher fidelity.

Fidelity ladder mapping: model_family -> [variant_full, variant_quantized, variant_condensed]. Maintain a small compatibility matrix for safe fallbacks between variants (tokenization/IO shape must be compatible).

Probabilistic thinning implemented with per-tenant seed and region-specific factor to avoid correlated drops across clients. Store seed in tenant profile to make thinning deterministic per-request sequence where needed.

Soft-borrowing exposes two counters: borrowed_budget_remaining (decrements on acceptance) and borrowed_budget_recovery (background replenish). Implement strict caps and admin override for incident response.

Circuit breaker thresholds are configurable via runtime flags (default: p95_latency > 1200ms and error_rate > 1% sustained for 2m). Breakers must emit structured events to Kafka and update /health endpoints for downstream controllers.
Add feature flag gating and per-tenant opt-out for embedding+canned fallbacks during canary to avoid surprising enterprise customers.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + admission simulator that replays production request trace to validate decisions against baseline; finish by 2026-03-17.
Phase 1 (canary): enable controller in eu-west-1 for 5% of traffic with borrowed_budget enabled for ap-southeast-1; monitor for 48h and validate acceptance criteria.
Phase 2 (regional expansion): enable in us-east-1 and eu-central with borrowed budgets; increase traffic to 25% while keeping P0/P1 safeguards on.
Phase 3 (full): global rollout with dashboards and runbook in place; enable auto-borrowing across configured pairs and remove per-tenant opt-outs after communication window.
Rollback: revert feature flag; borrowed_budget counters are ephemeral and will be discarded on rollback.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add dashboard: 'Admission Controller – Fidelity Breakdown' (panels: admitted_by_fidelity, admitted_by_tenant_band, rejected_rate).
Alert A1 (P0 latency breach): fire when any P0 tenant p95 > configured SLO for 5m — pager.
Alert A2 (borrow budget exhaustion): warn when borrowed_budget_remaining < 10% for more than 1m — page to oncall for capacity ops.
Alert A3 (circuit breaker open rate): page if > 3 breakers open across regions in 5m window.
Trace annotations: admission_reason, degradation_level, borrowed_region, kv_cache_hit must be included in 100% of sampled traces.
comments: 2026-03-10 – Ava Martinez: Initial triage and writeup. Observed repeated cascades during last APAC outage; baseline simulation shows 13% throughput loss if we only use strict token-bucket shedding.
2026-03-11 – Liam O'Connor: Design review notes — prefer Redis LUA for atomic borrowed_budget ops. Raised concern about cross-region consistency; propose eventual consistency with lease windows.
2026-03-12 – Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed monitoring plan. Suggested adding a per-tenant 'grace_credits' counter to preserve short bursts for VIP customers during borrow windows.
2026-03-13 – QA note: simulator run with 7 days of production trace shows 9.6% uplift in useful tokens served during simulated region failover when enabling kv-cache hinting; p0 unaffected.
2026-03-13 – Next: implement canary gating, add admin override and migrate per-tenant seeds to tenant-profile service.
